header.label: research
header.title: Variational Tensor Neural Networks: A Critical Analysis
header.lede: A close reading of a 2024 paper that trains tensor-network layers with an algorithm from quantum physics. It brings no breakthrough in compression or scalability; what is new is a combination, tensor layers trained like DMRG inside ordinary deep networks, that lets one read the network's entanglement while it trains.

decisions.title: Compression and hybrid stacks were already there
formula: M = U S V^\dagger = L R
decisions.caption: A weight matrix split by SVD; keeping the χ largest singular values λᵢ in S sets the bond dimension. Tensorised layers built this way date back to 2015.

decisions.title: What is new: variational training inside a hybrid network
decisions.caption: Two neighbouring tensors are merged into a bond tensor B, moved by a gradient step, then split again by SVD: the singular values come out at every step. E is the rest of the network. The article's Eq. (7), taken literally, climbs the loss; the consistent form is shown.

decisions.title: Interpretability while the network trains
decisions.caption: Entanglement entropy at a bond, from the normalised singular values. Gaussian blobs: S ≈ 0 at 99 % accuracy. Three spirals: S settles around 0.7–0.8 at about 95 %.

decisions.title: No case for scalability
decisions.caption: The TNN wins only the single-epoch comparison; Stoudenmire & Schwab's MPS classifier already reported under 1 % test error. Its training time per epoch grows exponentially with the number of MPO tensors.
